result.proposed_fix: Make the separator axis fail closed rather than adding more literals: (1) define a dot-like class generated from Unicode data (every char whose unicodedata name contains FULL STOP, DOT, MIDDLE DOT, BULLET, or ONE DOT LEADER, plus '.' U+3002 U+FF0E U+FF61), and accept it optionally wrapped in any bracket pair ([], (), {}, <>) or as the word 'dot', with \s* (not \s+) on EITHER side, and runs of them ('..', '\.'); (2) when whitespace touches the separator, keep the _SENTENCE_WORDS exception (and extend _is_domain so 'word .Then' stays text) but otherwise treat 'label SEP tld' as a link when tld is letters>=2 or ACE and is followed by a non-letter or '/'; (3) remove the {0,62} label cap (use [\w-]+); (4) in mask_links/has_link_or_contact also test each whitespace token and each pair of adjacent tokens after stripping edge punctuation, so the spaced forms are caught per token too; (5) add a generated regression test that loops over every Unicode code point whose name matches the dot-like set and over {'', ' '} x {'', ' '} spacing x bracket wrappers, asserting has_link_or_contact, mask_links, SY.verify (dropped LINK_OR_CONTACT), SY.extractive (not selected) and build_surface+require_valid (no host in dump), self-contained in one test file.
result.root_cause: uri_web/untrusted.py builds bare-domain detection as a positive allow-list of exact separator spellings: _DOT (line 69-70) accepts only '.', U+3002/U+FF0E/U+FF61, bracket/paren-wrapped '.'/'dot', and '\s+dot\s+' / '\s+\.\s+' (whitespace required on BOTH sides), and _BARE (line 71) additionally requires exact label shapes ([^\W_][\w-]{0,62}) and specific boundary classes. Any separator spelling not enumerated (one-sided space 'portal .com' / 'portal. com', U+00B7, U+0387, U+2027, U+2219, U+22C5, U+30FB, U+2E3C, '{.}', '<.>', '{dot}', '..', '\.', or a >63-char label) is not a separator, so the text is not a link. has_link_or_contact/mask_links fail open, and every caller (synthesize.verify:240, extractive:300/320, surface.clean:38, evaluate:287) trusts that single detector. R3-01 made only the TLD axis fail closed; the separator axis and (until R5) the boundary axis kept matching fixed lists. R5-01's specific forms are fixed at HEAD; the same class (R1-01) is still reproducible (R6-01).
result.why_earlier_repairs_failed: Each repair widened the regex by exactly the reviewer's examples and added regression tests that enumerate only those literals: ca622bc0 added [.] (.) [dot] (dot) (ASCII only); f3700643 added NFKC + three CJK full stops and introduced _BARE with (?<![\w-])/(?![\w-]) boundaries (the R5-01 bug); 462be42c added spaced defangs but wrote '\s+\.\s+' symmetric (test only has 'refundsportal . com'), leaving one-sided spacing open (R6-01); f5a5b8ec added only the xn-- TLD form; 29771992 changed only the boundary checks to (?<![^\W_])/(?![^\W_]) and tested only the reviewer's WRAPPED list. No repair replaced the enumeration with a fail-closed rule or tested a generated family of separators, so each round's suite passed while the next variant stayed open.
